column1: What does the computer actually receive when you type a prompt?
column2: A row of bytes: whole numbers from 0 to 255, one per plain-English character.
A piece of text (often a word or part of one) with its own id number. The model reads and writes tokens, never letters.

column1: How does Byte Pair Encoding (BPE) build its vocabulary?
column2: Start from the 256 bytes, then repeatedly glue together the most frequent pair of neighbouring tokens in the training text.

column1: Why is 'weather' one token but 'xylophone' eight?
column2: Merges are learned by frequency. Common strings earn their own token; rare ones are spelled from small pieces.
A table lookup: token id 559 selects row 559 of a learned table, giving a vector of 64 numbers.

column1: Why is a position vector added to each token vector?
column2: Attention sees all tokens at once, like a bag. Without positions, 'dog bites man' and 'man bites dog' would look the same.
The shared channel of token vectors flowing through the transformer. Every block reads it and ADDS its result; nothing overwrites it.

column1: What are the two halves of a transformer block?
column2: Attention (tokens exchange information) and a Multi-Layer Perceptron, MLP (each token is processed on its own).
Raw scores, one per vocabulary token, for what comes next. Softmax turns them into probabilities.

column1: In attention, what are the query, key and value?
column2: Query: what this token is looking for. Key: what each token contains. Value: what a token hands over when chosen.
The rule that a token may only attend to tokens before it, because during generation the future does not exist yet.

column1: What does the temperature knob do?
column2: Divides the logits before softmax. Low: the favourite nearly always wins. High: unlikely tokens get a chance. Zero: always the top token.

column1: How many forward passes does a 16-token answer take?
column2: About 17: one per generated token plus the one that produces the end token. Each pass runs the whole model.

column1: How does generation know when to stop?
column2: The model predicts a special <|end|> token, which it learned during alignment.
Reading a prediction off the residual stream after each layer, not just the last. It shows the answer forming layer by layer.
